config.title: TanStack Query Basics

intro.title: TanStack Query Basics
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Vue application that fetches and displays a list of posts from a mock API. You will learn the core concept of server-state management using TanStack Query (Vue Query) to handle data fetching, caching, and synchronization. The main technologies involved are Vue 3 with the Composition API, the TanStack Query Vue library, and JavaScript for logic. By the end, you'll understand how to efficiently load and update remote data in your Vue apps without manual state management.
intro.usecase: TanStack Query is essential for building data-driven Vue applications like e-commerce dashboards that display real-time sales metrics, inventory levels, and customer analytics. Developers use it in social media feeds to efficiently fetch, cache, and update posts, comments, and notifications without manual state management. It's also crucial for admin panels that manage user data, where paginated tables, filters, and search functionality require optimized server-state synchronization. This pattern eliminates repetitive loading/error logic, letting you focus on building responsive UIs that feel instant to users.

objectives: Initialize TanStack Query in a Vue application by installing dependencies and configuring the QueryClient
Implement data fetching with useQuery to retrieve and display API data in Vue components
Configure query options to control caching, retry behavior, and stale time for API requests
Manipulate query states to handle loading, error, and success scenarios in the UI
Integrate TanStack Query with Vue's reactive system to automatically update components when data changes
Construct a data fetching pattern that separates data logic from presentation components
Apply query invalidation to refresh data when user actions require updated information

steps.title: Import Vue and TanStack Query dependencies
steps.instruction: Import Vue, ref, and the required TanStack Query modules (useQuery, useQueryClient, QueryClient, VueQueryPlugin) from their respective packages.
steps.hint: You'll need to import from 'vue' and '@tanstack/vue-query'. Make sure to import all the listed symbols.

steps.hint: Use the QueryClient constructor from TanStack Query to create a new instance.

const myClient = new QueryClient();

steps.title: Create the main Vue component
steps.instruction: Create a Vue component named 'App' using the Options API with a setup function that returns an empty object, and include a template with a single root div.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can define a component using defineComponent. The setup function should return an object (even if empty for now). The template must have a single root element, like a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a basic Vue component named 'App' with a setup function and a template containing a root div.
successCriteria: The component is named 'App', uses defineComponent, has a setup function returning an empty object, and includes a template with a single root div.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your component is named 'App', uses defineComponent, has a setup function that returns an object, and includes a template with a single root div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component structure is incorrect. Ensure you're using defineComponent, the setup function returns an object, and the template has a single root element like a div.

steps.title: Initialize reactive state for manual refresh
steps.instruction: Inside your main Vue component, create a ref named 'refreshCounter' and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Use Vue's ref function to create reactive state. The ref should hold a number value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a reactive counter
const count = ref(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a reactive refreshCounter variable that can be incremented to trigger query refreshes.
successCriteria: The component contains a ref named 'refreshCounter' initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've created a ref named 'refreshCounter' with an initial value of 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires creating a ref named 'refreshCounter' initialized to 0. Check your syntax and try again.

steps.title: Define the data fetching function
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function of your App component, create an async function named fetchPosts that returns a promise resolving to mock post data.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses async/await or returns a Promise. You can simulate an API call with a setTimeout or return mock data directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an async function named fetchPosts that returns mock post data, ready to be used with TanStack Query.
successCriteria: An async function named fetchPosts is defined inside the setup function and returns a promise with mock data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure your function is named fetchPosts, uses async/await or returns a Promise, and returns mock data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The fetchPosts function is not properly defined. Check that it's inside the setup function, uses async/await or returns a Promise, and returns mock data.

steps.title: Set up the useQuery hook
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, call the useQuery hook with a query key and the fetchPosts function, destructuring the returned object into data, isLoading, and error variables.
steps.hint: The useQuery hook takes an object with queryKey and queryFn properties. Use the fetchPosts function as the queryFn.
steps.expectedOutcome: The useQuery hook is properly configured with queryKey and queryFn, and the returned object is destructured to access data, isLoading, and error.
successCriteria: useQuery is called with an object containing queryKey and queryFn, and the result is destructured into data, isLoading, and error variables.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling useQuery with both queryKey and queryFn, and destructuring the returned object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The useQuery hook setup is incomplete. Check that you're passing an object with queryKey and queryFn, and destructuring the result.

steps.title: Create the manual refresh handler
steps.instruction: Inside the setup function, define a function named handleRefresh that increments the refreshCounter value by 1.
steps.hint: You can define a function that uses the ref's .value property to update the counter.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a handleRefresh function that increments refreshCounter when called.
successCriteria: A function named handleRefresh is defined and increments refreshCounter.value by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a function, but make sure it increments refreshCounter.value by 1.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function is missing or doesn't properly increment the refresh counter. Try defining handleRefresh to update refreshCounter.value.
